Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
On 20 Aug 2002 20:04:25 -0700, take...@yahoo.com
(=?ISO-8859-1?Q?Dr._Enrique_Monta=F1o?=) wrote:

>I read the new tournament rule that excludes NRA restriction.
>Does it mean that I can bleed, untap, bleed, infinite times??

No.

The Camarilla Edition rules specifically prohibit this.

6.1.1 Bleed, page 21
A minion cannot perform more than one bleed action each turn, even if
he untaps.

Also, only one political action per turn:

6.1.7 Political Actions, page 25
A minion cannot perform more than one politcal action each turn.

Also, you cannot repeat an action card by name:

6.1.6 Action Card (or Card in Play), page 25
A minion cannot perform an action with the same action card or via the
same card in play (including from the minion's own card text) more
than once each turn, even if he untaps.

Notice also that Retainers, Equipment, and Allies are all subsets of
action cards (1.6.3.3, page 15), so that you cannot equip with the
same piece of equipment multiple times in the same turn, but your
crafty Ravnos can equip with a Laptop, untap, equip with a Treasured
Samadji, untap, employ Tasha Morgan, untap, employ J.S. Simmons, Esq.,
untap, and then attempt to bleed.

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

http://www.TheLasombra.com

> wouldn't 60 traps be better? sure, you're likely to go to torpor

> also, include 6 cards you actually want to have (sudden reversal,
> direct intervention, and 5 telepathic counters is good) and play with
> aus/AUS weenies, and it should be a go-er.

No, see, traps and Nosferatu Putrescence and whatever have vital flaws that
make the "Attempt to withdraw on your second turn" decks weak!

If you need to get into combat to play all of your cards, you also need:

A) A way to get into combat (Bum's Rush or something)
B) Someone to get into combat with.

(A) requires having enough of the Bum's Rush in your deck that you can
reasonably expect to draw one on the first turn, but not having enough so
that you can jam on them. As a result, you can only put 6 in your deck, and
even with 6 in a 60 card deck, it isn't impossible that you don't draw one
for a couple turns, at which point you are screwed.

(B) is completely beyond your control, and the hope is that your predator
won't get out a vampire till turn 3 (see, this isn't a *good* plan...).

With 60 Freak Drives and March Halcyan, you always get out a vampire on T1,
you always (ok, barring an interception, but who is going to intercept March
hunting?) run out your deck on T2. You just have to hope that your predator
doesn't have blasters...
